messages.author: f4a029f64dcdc43e
messages.subject: Stan 15.1 broken (for me) in Windows 10
parts:
I recently updated my R and RStan installations in Windows 10, and it broke RStan. I was previously using R 3.3.3 and RStan 2.14.2. When I updated, suddenly R would crash when I tried to run models that ran perfectly before. I tried uninstalling all versions of R, Rtools, and all R libraries, and reinstalling from scratch, but to no avail.

To be precise, this is what I've tried installing:
R 3.4
Rtools 3.4 (most recent version, notably non-frozen)
RStan 15.1

A minimal example of the problem in in the attached .stan and .R files. Basically, R crashes when you call stan() on a previously compiled model with a vector parameter with a dimension larger than 43, but only when you call stan() for the second time on that model. Stan compiles the model find and will sample from it as long as sampling is part of the same stan() call as compilation. But if I try to sample from a previously compiled model, R crashes. Interestingly, I have some saved Stan models compiled in my previous R/Rstan install (Stan 2.14.2 in R 3.3.3 with I believe Rtools 3.3). Saved in the sense that I called > save(fit, file = "fit.RData") in R, modulo the file/object names. If I load one of them into R 3.4 and use RStan 15.1 to sample from that model, I have zero problems.

Note: when R crashes, it gives the error code 255, though occasionally it will give the code 5.

Everything seems to work perfectly in Ubuntu with a fresh install of R 3.4 and RStan 15.1, so I suspect it has something to do with Rtools and the compiler it makes available.

Other things I've tried in Windows:

1) Install RStan 15.1 in R 3.3.3 using Rtools 3.3. This caused R to crash when the first time stan() was called on the model, though notably after compilation.
2) Install RStan 15.1 in R 3.4 using Rtools 3.4 from source. This threw an error - it had trouble installing RcppEigen for some reason (I don't have the error message recorded anywhere, sorry, but I believe it complained about the c++ compiler).

So I have two questions: 1) Is there a tweak to the installation process that will make everything work? Or, failing that, 2) How do I install an old version of RStan so I can get back to work?

Thanks,
Matt
